text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- World Jewish Congress Secretary General Elan Steinberg said Swiss diplomat Thomas Borer failed to stick to an agreement when he failed to choose Elie Wiesel to head the special Swiss Holocaust Fund.

- Decreasing construction in Switzerland led to a further 5.5 percent decline in cement orders in the first three months of the year compared to the previous quarter. Cement orders fell by 13 percent in 1996.
- Sales at pharmaceuticals giant Novartis rose by 22 percent to 8.2 billion Swiss francs in 1996.
- The Swiss government rejected calls to freeze bank accounts belonging to Zaire president Mobutu Sese Seko.

- Technology group Sulzer reported a 10 percent increase in orders to 1.64 billion Swiss francs in the 1997 first quarter. - Schweizerische Industrie Gesellschaft (SIG) expects a two-figure rise in sales and profit for the year.
